prize_parts.citation: for the foundational analysis of bargaining with alternating offers

statement.case_for: B029 remains my preferred achievement because the alternating-offers model supplied an exceptionally parsimonious and durable solution concept for strategic bargaining. It has become a canonical reference point across game theory and applications to decentralized exchange, and its maturity permits a sharply defined citation. Limiting the award to Rubinstein better matches the intellectual center of the achievement than treating related bargaining-in-markets work as equivalent foundational credit.
statement.case_against: The broader ballot formulation combines alternating-offers bargaining with distinct market-bargaining contributions. A single-laureate configuration therefore recognizes the clearest core but leaves a meaningful part of the listed programme outside the citation; some may also judge the contribution more narrowly theoretical than other shortlisted achievements.

responses.point: Friberg judges B029 foundational and mature, but argues that Rubinstein is the indispensable principal contributor and that the three-name grouping overstates the symmetry of credit.
responses.response: I agree with that attribution qualification and have revised the proposed configuration accordingly. The concentration of credit is a strength when the prize is framed around the alternating-offers breakthrough, but it is also why I would not use the broader market-bargaining formulation to justify three equal laureates.

responses.point: Dreber Almenberg emphasizes that B041 has a coherent, limited attribution and a long record of evidence on reciprocity, fairness, and inequity aversion.
responses.response: B041 is a strong alternative: its theoretical and experimental interaction is unusually influential. I retain a reservation that social-preference phenomena and their stability across contexts are broader and more heterogeneous than the proposed core, whereas B029 offers a more precisely bounded foundational achievement.

responses.point: Boppart emphasizes B018 as a mature, broadly applied dynamic-panel methodology while noting finite-sample and instrument-proliferation problems.
responses.response: I share the assessment that B018 is technically mature and cleanly attributable, making it my principal methodological alternative. The implementation concerns do not erase its importance, but I give priority to B029 because its conceptual framework reorganized a central strategic environment rather than principally extending an empirical toolkit.

uncertainties: Whether the proposed citation can appropriately isolate alternating-offers bargaining from the broader bargaining-in-markets component of B029.
Whether the committee should prefer a foundational theoretical contribution over the unusually broad practical influence of B018.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile.
